zeros-and-poles.summary: $(z^2 - 1)/(z^2 + 1)$ coloured over the plane: zeros at $\pm 1$ (dark, every hue once) and poles at $\pm i$ (light).

cube.summary: $z^3$: one zero at the origin where every hue appears three times round.

exp.summary: $e^z$ on a wide view: hue repeats every $2\pi$ up the imaginary axis, lightness grows to the right.
